question: Ticket e1fb0e0bc945 says 'withdrawn questions stop holding the build (resolved=True, answer=None) even when not answered by an operator', but outline 9.3.5.1 reads "Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a question on the ticket, which holds its build until answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing." (The outline states: 'An open question in those sections... becomes a question on the ticket, which holds its build until answered.' The ticket allows questions to stop holding the build without being answered—contradicting the 'until answered' condition. The outline treats 'answered' as the sole mechanism to clear the hold; the ticket adds withdrawal as an alternative path that bypasses this requirement.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: Both stand; they do not conflict. A duplicate is the same question asked twice. Withdrawing one copy leaves the kept copy open, and the kept copy holds the build until it is answered, so the build still waits on an answer, as 9.3.5.1 says. Measured: tooth 1 of cairn/tools/question/proofs/test_a_duplicate_question_is_withdrawn_unanswered.py asserts open_for(ticket) still lists the kept question after the withdrawal, and withdraw refuses a keeper that is itself withdrawn (tooth 2), so the last copy of a question cannot be withdrawn.
